definition: The whole amount; every person or thing.
quote: “All the world’s a stage, and all the men and women merely players.”
speaker: Jaques
note: A reflection on life as a performance.

definition: The quality of expressing much in few words.
quote: “Brevity is the soul of wit.”
speaker: Polonius
note: A witty reminder that concise speech can be powerful.

definition: People who lack courage in the face of danger.
quote: “Cowards die many times before their deaths; the valiant never taste of death but once.”
speaker: Caesar
note: A contrast between fear and courage.

definition: To question or feel uncertain about something.
quote: “Doubt thou the stars are fire, doubt that the sun doth move.”
speaker: Hamlet
note: A dramatic expression of certainty in love.

definition: “And you, Brutus?”—an expression of shocked betrayal.
quote: “Et tu, Brute? Then fall, Caesar!”
speaker: Caesar
note: A famous moment of betrayal.

definition: Weakness or the quality of being easily damaged.
quote: “Frailty, thy name is woman!”
speaker: Hamlet
note: Hamlet’s bitter lament about human weakness.

definition: To present or offer something to someone.
quote: “Give every man thy ear, but few thy voice.”
speaker: Polonius
note: Advice about listening thoughtfully.

definition: High respect, integrity, or a strong sense of what is right.
quote: “Mine honour is my life; both grow in one.”
speaker: Mowbray
note: Honour is presented as inseparable from identity.

definition: Used to introduce a condition or possibility.
quote: “If music be the food of love, play on.”
speaker: Orsino
note: A lyrical opening to a meditation on love.

definition: Fear or suspicion that someone may be unfaithful or disloyal.
quote: “O, beware, my lord, of jealousy; it is the green-eyed monster.”
speaker: Iago
note: A vivid metaphor for destructive jealousy.

definition: The quality of being friendly, generous, and considerate.
quote: “Kindness in women, not their beauteous looks, shall win my love.”
speaker: Suffolk
note: A line that values character over appearance.

definition: A deep affection or strong feeling of care.
quote: “Love looks not with the eyes, but with the mind.”
speaker: Helena
note: Love is described as an inward way of seeing.

definition: The unlawful killing of a person; in Shakespeare, often a sign of treachery and moral disorder.
quote: “Murder most foul, as in the best it is; but this most foul, strange, and unnatural.”
speaker: Ghost
note: The Ghost describes the killing of King Hamlet.

definition: Not anything; no thing at all.
quote: “Nothing will come of nothing.”
speaker: Lear
note: A stark statement about action and consequence.

definition: On one occasion; at a particular time in the past.
quote: “Once more unto the breach, dear friends, once more.”
speaker: Henry V
note: A stirring call to courage and resolve.

definition: The act of leaving or saying goodbye.
quote: “Parting is such sweet sorrow.”
speaker: Juliet
note: A tender phrase that holds sadness and affection together.

definition: A characteristic or feature of someone or something.
quote: “The quality of mercy is not strained.”
speaker: Portia
note: Mercy is described as something freely given.

definition: To keep something in one’s mind; to recall.
quote: “Remember thee? Ay, thou poor ghost, while memory holds a seat in this distracted globe.”
speaker: Hamlet
note: Hamlet vows not to forget his father’s ghost.

definition: An unspecified number or amount.
quote: “Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon ’em.”
speaker: Malvolio, reading
note: A playful reflection on the different paths to greatness.

definition: To exist or live; the central phrase in Hamlet’s soliloquy.
quote: “To be, or not to be: that is the question.”
speaker: Hamlet
note: The opening of one of literature’s best-known soliloquies.

definition: Anxious, troubled, or not at ease.
quote: “Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.”
speaker: King Henry IV
note: A king reflects on the burden of responsibility.

definition: Moral goodness or admirable qualities.
quote: “Virtue is bold, and goodness never fearful.”
speaker: Duke Vincentio
note: A confident statement about moral courage.

definition: Experiences or images of the mind during sleep; also hopes and visions.
quote: “We are such stuff as dreams are made on.”
speaker: Prospero
note: A poetic reflection on the fleeting nature of life.

definition: The name of Socrates’ wife, used in the play as a classical allusion.
quote: “As old as Sibyl, and as curst and shrewd as Socrates’ Xanthippe, or a worse.”
speaker: Petruchio
note: A classical reference used in Petruchio’s comic boast.

definition: The period of life when someone is young.
quote: “Youth’s a stuff will not endure.”
speaker: Feste
note: A brief reflection on the passing of youth.

definition: An old exclamation expressing surprise or anger.
quote: “Zounds, where thou wilt, lad. I’ll make one.”
speaker: Falstaff
note: A lively example of an Elizabethan exclamation.
